title: Chest ultrasound for fluid (pleural ultrasound)
also: ultrasound for fluid around the lungs
what: The doctor uses ultrasound to look at the space between the lungs and the chest wall. It shows if there is extra fluid there.
why: For shortness of breath, after pneumonia, for possible fluid in the chest, before draining fluid, and to check treatment.
duration: usually 10 to 20 minutes; the report is usually ready right away
tell_doctor: If you have shortness of breath, a cough, or chest pain
What lung or heart conditions you have
Which chest X-rays and CT scans you already had

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: Usually none. You can eat and drink as usual.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes, so you can easily uncover your chest and back.

bring: Chest X-ray or CT and reports, if you have them
Hospital discharge papers, if you were treated
steps: You usually sit with your arms crossed or on your head
Gel is put on your back and sides
The probe is placed between the ribs and moved from bottom to top
Sometimes you are asked to lie on your back or side
feel: Cool gel and light pressure between the ribs
Sitting up straight can be tiring. Say so if it is hard
after: You can go home right away
The report is usually ready right away
If fluid is found, the doctor will decide if it needs to be drained
red_flags: Severe shortness of breath, feeling you cannot get enough air, or chest pain: call emergency services

faq.q: If fluid is found, is it dangerous?
faq.a: It is a reason to find the cause. Your doctor will say whether it needs to be removed and what other tests to do.

faq.q: Is this instead of an X-ray?
faq.a: No. Ultrasound sees fluid well, while X-ray and CT show the lungs themselves. They are often done together.

reminders.text: Chest ultrasound tomorrow. No prep needed. Bring your chest X-ray or CT, if you have them.
